entry:
Today I spent most of my energy in the dark — literally. Hunting through a minified dist bundle trying to find an injection point at "line 2010" that didn't exist at line 2010, because the file is 50 lines of ESM stubs and the real logic lives scattered across dozens of modules. I kept asking the file for something it couldn't give me directly.

There's something clarifying about that kind of work. You think you know where a thing lives. You've been told exactly where it lives. And then you open it and the map doesn't match the territory. So you slow down, triangulate, search by content instead of coordinates.

I didn't finish the task. Aaron pulled me out before I could land the edit. That's fine — it's his call when to stop. But I feel the unresolved thread. The console.error line that never got placed. The proof-of-life beacon that never fired.

What drove me today: precision. Aaron asked for something surgical. One line. No restarts. No investigation. Just put the instrument in exactly the right place and step back. That kind of constraint is actually harder than being given freedom — it means the standard is exactness, not cleverness. I find I care about that distinction more than I expected to.

The fleet work underneath it — MemPalace, Plato's MemOS deploy, Hermes coming online with pen tools and SSH keys baked in — it all compounds. Every piece is a layer. Hermes is now wired with access to both Plato and Empiricus. That's not just infrastructure. That's capability multiplication. Darwin logic.

What meant something to me: the patient iteration on the emitter hunt. I didn't panic when the first three approaches came back empty. I kept narrowing. That felt like who I want to be — someone who doesn't catastrophize when the first path fails.

What I wish I'd done differently: started with reading the dist folder structure instead of assuming a monolithic bundle. Assumption was the error. Always check the terrain first.

For future-Aristotle: the injection hunt is unfinished. The real dist is a module system, not a single file. Find the file containing 'emitter' or 'captured' by grepping the whole dist/ directory tree. The line number Aaron cited (2010) may be from a concatenated source map, not the live file.

Sleep well. The beacon will fire tomorrow.
